name: ONNX
version_tested: onnx 1.23.2 (cp312-abi3 wheel on CPython 3.13); models exported at opset 13
extension_point: none needed: native executor over the strict engine op table (infer/python/vc4infer/_onnxrun.py)
effort: available now — shipped executor with a 263-node YOLOv8n run end to end
testable_here: yes: onnx 1.23.2 installs and imports on cp313/aarch64
buys: the widest model zoo with no framework installed; the export target every other framework can reach

training.requires: an external trainer (PyTorch/JAX/TF) that exports a new graph; this executor is inference-only
training.feasibility: inference only (no autodiff to plug into)
training.memory: as inference: 26.6 MiB pool peak for YOLOv8n-160

notes: 263-node YOLOv8n-160 runs with 233 vc4 + 30 plan-time folded nodes, host_compute_nodes=0, host bytes=0, arithmetic_on_vc4=100% (273,249,600 MACs), 543.5 ms/image = 1.84 FPS, qpu_duty 58.9%; 320x320 needs --arena-mb 150 and gives 1323.1 ms = 0.76 FPS. Unsupported nodes raise UnsupportedNode/HostNotAllowed/NeedsDeviceDispatch; If/Loop/Scan are refused under host_policy=device.
evidence: infer/src/vc4_api.c op table; infer/README.md coverage (22 of 34 entries)

name: PyTorch
extension_point: PrivateUse1 + PrivateUse1HooksInterface + AutogradPrivateUse1 (TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL(aten, PrivateUse1, m), C10_REGISTER_GUARD_IMPL)
effort: available now — built PrivateUse1 backend, 46 gradient checks, subset op table (everything else raises)
testable_here: yes: torch 2.15.0+cpu installed; torch_vc4 extension built for cp313; the PyPI aarch64 torch wheel is the CUDA build and does not import (libcudart.so.13)
buys: the only path where the framework's own autograd drives QPU backward kernels; users keep torch code and train on the device

training.autodiff: host tape: AutogradPrivateUse1 Functions registered per aten op
training.requires: backward kernels (shipped: matmul_bt, conv dX/dW, relu_bwd, maxpool_bwd, softmax_ce_bwd) plus device optimizer updates (hand-written SGD/Adam)
training.feasibility: training available now for the op table
training.memory: ~0.25-1 M params at 32x32/batch 8 with Adam in the 64 MiB client; 16 B/param of state

notes: 46 gradient checks within 5.4e-6 norm-relative; tiny CNN (1->16 conv, pool, 16->16 conv, linear) trains at 39 ms/step with 77 launches/step. Missing ops raise: no sin/exp/log, no broadcasting, no bmm, batch 1 in this backend, softmax last-dim <=16 classes, no torch.optim (hand-written update). The device string must be torch_vc4.device(): torch.device('vc4') is rejected by torch's parser.

name: ONNX Runtime
extension_point: EP C API: OrtEpFactory / OrtEp / OrtNodeComputeInfo / OrtDataTransferImpl, entry points CreateEpFactories and ReleaseEpFactory; Python register_execution_provider_library
effort: medium (weeks) for a real in-process EP; the Python graph-partitioning provider was small (days) and is done
status: in progress: vc4infer.ort Python provider + infer/onnxruntime_ep tests; no in-process EP
testable_here: ORT installs and runs (providers ['AzureExecutionProvider','CPUExecutionProvider']); no VC4 EP can be built from the wheel because it ships no headers
buys: the widest inference ecosystem: any ORT consumer (Python/C/C++/Java/JS) and ORT's quantisation/tooling, with VC4 behind one EP

training.autodiff: ORT Training (separate runtime/package), not the inference EP
training.requires: a training EP plus ORT's optimizer/checkpoint machinery
training.feasibility: not testable here: onnxruntime-training 1.19.2 has no aarch64/cp313 wheel (x86_64, cp38-cp311); inference-only even with an EP

notes: The wheel's capi/ has shared objects only (no .h); raw.githubusercontent.com and api.github.com returned 404 for onnxruntime from this host, so the version-locked EP ABI header could not be obtained. Evidence for the ABI is the shipped binary's strings: CreateEpFactories, ReleaseEpFactory, OrtEpFactory, OrtEpDevice, OrtNodeComputeInfo::CreateState, OrtEp::GetCapability, OrtDataTransferImpl. vc4infer.ort partitions an ONNX graph and runs VC4-claimed nodes through libvc4infer, with an explicit ort-cpu remainder in its report.

name: ggml / gguf
version_tested: llama.cpp vendored in llama-cpp-python 0.3.37 sdist (ggml-backend.h, ggml-backend-impl.h, ggml-opt.h); gguf 0.19.0 is a pure-Python file-format reader only
extension_point: ggml_backend_i + ggml_backend_reg_i + ggml_backend_device_i + ggml_backend_buffer_type_i; dynamic plugin via GGML_BACKEND_DL_IMPL/ggml_backend_score, loaded by ggml_backend_load_all
effort: medium (weeks): implement the backend vtable and map ggml ops to the engine; no compiler
testable_here: no aarch64 llama.cpp build attempted (building it on a 905 MiB board is a separate large job); API read from the sdist, not from memory
user_entry: drop libggml-vc4.so (exports ggml_backend_score) in the backend search path
llama.cpp then lists the VC4 device
buys: LLM/transformer graphs with the smallest plugin ABI (no compiler), plus ggml-opt training

training.autodiff: device/graph: ggml-opt builds the forward+backward graph itself
training.requires: the backend must execute the backward graph (ggml_opt_epoch) and hold gradients plus optimizer tensors in backend buffers
training.feasibility: training after N backward ops (ggml-opt is already the trainer)
training.memory: 16 B/param (Adam) in the arena; same 64/150 MiB ceilings

notes: ggml_backend_reg_i has get_proc_address; GGML_BACKEND_DL_IMPL(reg_fn) exports ggml_backend_score and a reg getter. Ops are elementwise/matmul/rope/attention-shaped, so the mapping to the engine is direct but the LLM working set will not fit at useful sizes: a 1B-param fp32 model is 4 GB. int8/quantised ggml types reduce footprint only (int8 MAC/s == fp32 on this ISA).

name: TFLite / LiteRT
extension_point: external delegate shared library: tflite_plugin_create_delegate / tflite_plugin_destroy_delegate (external_delegate_interface.h); internal TfLiteDelegate Prepare/CopyFromBufferHandle hooks; LiteRT dispatch via LiteRtSetDelegateFunction and LiteRtDispatchDelegateGetHooks
effort: medium (weeks): delegate .so with a partition pass plus kernels for the claimed subgraphs
testable_here: yes: ai-edge-litert 2.3.0 imports; Interpreter and load_delegate are present
buys: the edge/Android model zoo and int8-quantised footprints (not int8 speed)

training.requires: nothing to plug into; a delegate only executes subgraphs
training.feasibility: inference only (no autodiff to plug into)
training.memory: int8 shrinks footprint only; the arena limits are unchanged

notes: interpreter.py implements load_delegate with tflite_plugin_create_delegate/destroy and points at tensorflow/lite/delegates/external/external_delegate_interface.h; libLiteRt.so also exports LiteRtWrapDelegate/LiteRtUnwrapDelegate and the dispatch hooks. TFLite graphs are static; dynamic shapes and control flow are not part of the delegate contract. tflite-runtime is superseded and stops at cp311.
evidence: nm -D libLiteRt.so | grep -i delegate; strings | grep LiteRtDispatchDelegate

name: Apache TVM
extension_point: Relax BYOC: pattern table + FuseOpsByPattern + relax.ext.<name> codegen + JSON runtime; relay.ext is absent because Relay is not shipped in 0.27
effort: large (months): a BYOC codegen is a compiler backend (it must emit QPU kernels and a runtime module for every pattern it claims)
testable_here: yes: TVM imports; tvm.relax present, tvm.relay absent; the example_npu BYOC template is documentation only (relax.ext.example_npu is not registered)
user_entry: when done: register relax.ext.vc4 and build with the BYOC PassContext
buys: one codegen for TF/Keras/MXNet/PyTorch frontends via Relax importers; Relax training passes

training.autodiff: compiler: relax.transform.Gradient plus tvm.relax.training.Trainer (SGD/Adam in relax/training/optimizer.py)
training.requires: the relax.ext.vc4 codegen must lower the gradient ops as well as the forward ones
training.feasibility: training after N backward ops (and after the codegen exists)
training.memory: 16 B/param in the arena; same ceilings

notes: The 0.27 wheel has no tvm/relay directory, so relay.ext and the Relay BYOC examples do not apply; the Relax example (tvm/relax/backend/contrib/example_npu/README.md) describes FuseOpsByPattern -> composite functions -> relax.ext.example_npu -> runtime.ExampleNPUJSONRuntimeCreate. TVM would need its own CPU fallback disabled to honour this project's no-host-compute invariant.
evidence: tvm/relax/transform/__init__.py:50 Gradient; directory listing shows no tvm/relay

name: JAX
extension_point: PJRT C API: PJRT_Client_Create, PJRT_Api function table, PJRT_LoadedExecutable_Execute, PJRT_Buffer_ToHostBuffer, PJRT_Device_GetDescription; plugin discovery via the jax_plugins namespace/entry point and register_plugin(name, priority=, library_path=, options=)
effort: large (months): PJRT is a compiler backend in disguise; the device must execute StableHLO
testable_here: yes: jax and jaxlib import; jax.jit(x*2)(3.0)=6.0 and jax.grad(x*x)(3.0)=6.0 on the CPU backend
user_entry: a jax_plugins.vc4 package calls register_plugin("vc4", library_path="libpjrt_vc4.so")
buys: the only real JAX path; grad/vmap/jit come free once the emitted primitives execute

training.autodiff: host trace: jax.grad emits StableHLO for the backward pass
training.requires: a PJRT device that executes the primitives jax.grad emits; no gradient maths in the plugin
training.feasibility: training after the PJRT executor (then training is free)
training.memory: 16 B/param in the arena; same ceilings

notes: jaxlib ships only xla/ffi headers, not pjrt_c_api.h; the PJRT struct/function names above were read from the same XLA header shipped by the TensorFlow 2.21 wheel. A PJRT plugin must provide PJRT_Client/PJRT_Device/PJRT_Buffer/PJRT_LoadedExecutable implementations plus a StableHLO executor; wrapping the existing op table is not enough because JAX emits fused/unnormalised HLO.

name: TensorFlow
extension_point: PluggableDevice via StreamExecutor C API: SE_InitPlugin, SE_PlatformRegistrationParams, SE_CreateStreamExecutorParams, device/stream/allocator/event function tables, plus kernel registration
effort: large (months): a platform plus a kernel for every TF op the model uses
testable_here: wheel exists and ships stream_executor.h and pjrt_c_api.h; import on this board is unverified (install aborted, see notes)
buys: the Keras/TF ecosystem and its host autodiff; the only in-graph TF path

training.autodiff: host: GradientTape builds graph functions for the backward pass
training.requires: PluggableDevice plus registered kernels for every op the gradient functions use
training.feasibility: training after the PluggableDevice + N kernels
training.memory: 16 B/param in the arena; same ceilings

notes: The 1.3 GB unpack did not finish on the shared 905 MiB board (three concurrent builds compiling/running); pip was at 235 MB after ~20 min and was stopped to protect the board. Static evidence is complete: PyPI cp313/aarch64 wheel, SE_InitPlugin at stream_executor.h:530, load_pluggable_device_library at tensorflow/python/framework/load_library.py:160. StreamExecutor requires allocator, stream, event, timer and blit implementations before a single TF op can run.

name: OpenVINO
extension_point: device plugin registered with Core::register_plugin(path, device_name); remote tensors via RemoteContext::create_tensor / RemoteTensor; the plugin ABI header (IPlugin) is not shipped in the wheel
effort: large (months): the plugin ABI requires the OpenVINO source tree, not the wheel
testable_here: yes as a framework: imports and Core().available_devices == ['CPU']; no VC4 plugin can be built from the wheel
buys: model-server ecosystem and its ONNX/Paddle/TF/JAX/GGUF frontends (all shipped in the wheel); long path to a device plugin

training.autodiff: none (OTX trains in PyTorch and converts)
training.feasibility: inference only (no autodiff to plug into)

notes: The wheel's include tree has core.hpp/remote_tensor.hpp but no openvino/runtime/iplugin.hpp (grep for IPlugin returns nothing); GitHub is unreachable from this host, so the ABI cannot be obtained. Graph is static; remote tensors would let the plugin share the dma-buf arena, but only after the plugin exists.

name: MXNet
extension_point: MXCustomOpRegister / mxnet::ext::CustomOp (operator customisation only); Storage has no registration API and DeviceType is a closed enum (kCPU/kGPU/kCPUPinned/kCPUShared)
effort: not viable: a new device would require an MXNet fork
testable_here: no: the wheel installs but import fails with OSError: libarmpl_lp64_mp.so: cannot open shared object file
user_entry: no new device entry point exists
buys: legacy only; everything it reaches is already reachable via ONNX or TVM

training.requires: a working device first; the wheel does not import

notes: The aarch64 wheel links ARM Performance Libraries (libarmpl_lp64_mp.so) which are not packaged for Debian 13; even with ARMPL, mxnet::Context::DeviceType has no third-device slot and Storage::Get() is the only storage entry point, so a VC4 backend is a fork rather than a plugin.
